w: Locals call it Te Tapu-nui, mountain of intense sacredness. Below the 907m summit, wilding conifers give way to tussock and native cover. A working farm on the slopes has run 1,800 sheep since the Middleton family bought the lease in 1963 and freeholded the land in 1978.
s: 907m sacred peak still grazed by 1,800 sheep
_facts: Māori name Te Tapu-nui, 'mountain of intense sacredness'
Middleton family farm: 1,800 sheep, leased 1963, freeholded 1978
Time Walk track crosses the upper slopes

w: Named after the Scottish original by early shepherd Duncan McAusland, this 1,748m summit sits about 4km northwest of Queenstown's centre and delivers a 360-degree panorama: Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, Cecil Peak and Walter Peak all at once. Bowen Peak (1,631m) and Bob's Peaks flank it.
s: 360-degree summit view over the whole Wakatipu Basin
_facts: Named after Ben Lomond, Scotland, by shepherd Duncan McAusland
1,748m summit, about 4km northwest of Queenstown centre
360-degree panorama: Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, Cecil Peak, Walter Peak
Connected peaks: Bowen Peak (1,631m) and Bob's Peaks

w: Gourmet hamburgers built around fillings well outside the usual beef patty: lamb, cod, falafel, a swine-and-chicken mix, and venison all sit on the menu. Fergburger specialises in this style of loaded, gourmet-built burger at its Queenstown restaurant.
s: Gourmet burgers running to venison, cod and falafel
_facts: Burger fillings include lamb, cod, falafel, a swine-and-chicken mix, and venison
